Development at the Hinda phosphate project
POINTE-NOIRE, REPUBLIC OF CONGO
– Kropz plc (AIM: KRPZ) Chief Executive Officer Louis R. Loubser today announced the progress of the construction on the box cut for the proposed Hinda phosphate mine in the Republic of Congo’s, 40 km from Pointe-Noire outskirt.
The box cut construction contract was awarded to local companies, with the operation supervised by mining engineers, a market-leading, privately owned opencast contract mining company that specializes in medium- to large-scale surface mining and earthworks. The project is supported by the Cominco and Kropz teams.
Construction of the box cut, expected to take approximately two to three months, has made significant progress in the first few weeks. The box cut, developed in the mineral zone, is the initial excavation made in the opencast mine to expose the orebody deposit.
“This first development step is an important milestone in Cominco’s schedule to begin realising the large potential of the Hinda project’s vast resource, delivering meaningful benefits to our stakeholders,” said Mr Loubser.
The box cut objective is to obtain extensive technical data ahead of the next phase. “We are all very excited to expose the various layers of our deposit over a height of greater than 20 meters“, Mr Loubser added.
​
View of the box cut under construction in the Southern section of the orebody
In addition, a geologist has arrived in Pointe-Noire and is preparing the sampling campaign. Around 10 tonnes of samples will be shipped to South Africa where metallurgical testings will be carried out at our laboratory of sister company Elandsfontein.
Mr. Loubser said it is also important for Cominco to confirm the process for the
project which will guarantee the correct specification of the plant equipment to be purchased.
About Kropz
Kropz, with offices in South Africa and Congo, is advancing its Hinda phosphate project, considered as one of the largest undeveloped phosphate resources in Africa. Industry experts recognize that Hinda is a world-class phosphate deposit, both in terms of size and grade.
Kropz offers an unparalleled, Africa-based investment opportunity in the development, mining and processing - to the highest environmental, social and governance standards – of rock phosphate.

Strategic Update
Kropz Plc (AIM: KRPZ), an emerging African phosphate producer and developer, announces that it has begun an urgent operational review and restructuring process at Kropz Elandsfontein (Pty) Ltd
("Elandsfontein")
.
Since the announcement on 15 July 2026, there has continued to be significant financial pressure on the operations arising predominantly from the continued Middle East conflict. The disruption to key fertilizer inputs has adversely affected global fertilizer production and demand for phosphate rock, resulting in downward pressure on sales prices. Simultaneously, increases in fuel, chemical and freight costs have significantly affected the operating costs of the
Elandsfontein operations.
Over the past five months, the combined effect of lower realised sales prices and increased operating costs, together with the production ramp up being challenging, has resulted in Elandsfontein continuing to not achieve operational profitability. These conditions have necessitated an urgent operational review and the implementation of a restructuring process.
This operational review and restructuring process will result in a reduction of revenue generated from phosphate rock ("Phosrock") .During the first five months of the financial year ending 31 March 2027, Elandsfontein produced 150,246 tonnes of Phosrock with sales of 149,907 tonnes. Going forward, Phosrock revenue is expected to be generated primarily from the sale of existing stock on hand, with no further Phosrock production currently planned. The business will instead focus on the development and growth of the Nanophos market. While Nanophos sales volumes are expected to be lower than the historical volumes achieved from Phosrock, the strategy is intended to establish a more sustainable operating model with a lower cost base.
Nanophos is a natural sedimentary soft rock phosphate, rich in phosphate minerals, calcium and silica, used as a slow-release organic fertilizer to improve soil phosphate levels and promote long-term plant productivity. Unlike synthetic fertilizers, which can cause water pollution and soil degradation, soft rock phosphate is a natural product that supports sustainable farming practices. Its slow-release properties minimize the risk of nutrient leaching into water bodies, helping to protect precious natural resources.
Louis Loubser CEO of Kropz commented:
"The restructuring and operational downsizing process will be challenging and we understand the impact it will have on employees and their families and other stakeholders and are deeply saddened. The decision to undertake these actions has not been taken lightly and certainly not been easy. However, considering the continued financial pressures facing the Elandsfontein operation over several years, this initiative is necessary to establish a more sustainable operating model."
While Nanophos represents a new and developing market, sales to date have been constrained by production and material handling limitations. As a result of the operational review and restructuring process, management intends to increase its focus on Nanophos market development. Revenue is therefore expected to gain greater momentum over the coming months, subject to normal seasonality and the successful growth of the Nanophos customer base and market. Subject to board approval, Phosrock operations will re-start once market conditions have normalised.
The Company
believe that Nanophos has the prospect to be a significant contributor to the phosphate market in South Africa and provide a much needed solution to the needs of South African farming communities. The management team is committed to developing this prospect.
Louis Loubser CEO of Kropz further commented:
"While the transition will be challenging these actions are in the best interest of the business and its stakeholders. This long-term vision ultimately necessitated difficult decisions in the short term, and the Company will manage the process responsibly and provide the necessary notices in terms of the MPRDA to the Minister of the Department of Mineral Resources and Energy. Kropz will continue to provide updates on material developments as appropriate."

Kropz Plc (AIM: KRPZ), an emerging African phosphate producer and developer, announces that it will hold its Annual General Meeting ("AGM") at the offices of Haynes Boone, Alder Castle, 10 Noble Street, London EC2V 7JX on 24 September 2026 at 12:00 noon. The full Notice of Annual General Meeting (the "Notice") will be available on the Company's website
www.kropz.com
and is being posted to shareholders today, together with a Form of Proxy.
It should, however, be noted that completion of the audit of the Annual Report and Financial Statements for the year ended 31 March 2026 (the "2026 Accounts") is currently in progress and it has not been possible to publish these prior to the issue of this Notice. Therefore no resolution to receive and adopt the 2026 Accounts is being proposed at the AGM.
The Company expects to publish its 2026 Accounts by no later than 30 September 2026. Following the publication of the 2026 Accounts, a separate general meeting will be held later in the year at which such a resolution will be proposed.

company_30s.what_they_do: KRPZ is a phosphate exploration and development company focused on the Hinda project in the Republic of Congo. It works on drilling, feasibility studies and eventually mining operations to produce phosphate rock for the fertilizer market.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Phosphate is a core ingredient for global fertilizer, and demand is rising as food security becomes a priority. The Hinda project sits on a sizeable, relatively untapped deposit that could position KRPZ as a new supply source in a market dominated by a few large producers.
company_30s.current_state: The company is still in the early, high‑cost stage of development. It has drawn down bridge loans, secured a new loan facility and recently changed its nominated adviser, all signs of a company trying to shore up cash flow. Revenue is not yet generated and the business is still burning capital, but it is actively working to secure financing and move the project forward.

rns_narrative: KRPZ has been busy with project milestones: a new development update on the Hinda phosphate site, a strategic update, and a fresh loan facility that could extend cash runway.

The company is also dealing with corporate governance changes – a new nominated adviser and a note that ARC, which owns 85%, is still lending. That suggests ARC may be eyeing a private takeover to cut AIM costs once the project reaches break‑even.
Overall, the narrative is one of a company that is still in the survival phase but is making concrete moves to secure funding and demonstrate progress on the main asset.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Silence with a glimmer of hope
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls see the Hinda project as a hidden gem and believe ARC’s stake could bring the capital needed to get the mine off the ground.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the company’s heavy debt load, lack of revenue and the possibility of a takeover or delisting could crush the stock.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The chatter is still mostly neutral, but the repeated bullish posts about the Hinda project suggest a slow, positive shift that could tip the balance once a concrete milestone is announced.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – the market has not yet noticed KRPZ, giving a contrarian edge when a catalyst hits.

near_term_catalysts: A drilling or feasibility report that shows commercial viability of the Hinda deposit.
Approval of the new loan facility or a refinancing that improves the balance sheet.
A formal announcement that ARC intends to take the company private to reduce AIM costs.
Any technical trigger such as a volume spike above the 5‑day average or the price breaking its 20‑day moving average.
expect_next.watch_for: Positive drilling results, loan approval, a jump in daily volume, and a move above the 20‑day moving average are the key signals that would confirm the mean‑reversion thesis.
expect_next.timing_regime: The APEX score of 8.0 suggests a tight compression, indicating the market is still in the early stages of the recovery. The company appears to be in the early capitulation phase – the next catalyst could start the bounce.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The stock has already fallen deep into a 70‑95% crash zone. If it rebounds to halfway between the current price and its all‑time high, the return would be roughly 200‑300% relative to the current level. The mean‑reversion pattern for this colour of signal historically delivers massive upside, while the downside is limited to the current price if the company fails to recover.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The main risks are continued cash burn, high debt, and the possibility of ARC taking the company private or the company being delisted. A worst‑case scenario is a price collapse to zero, wiping out the entire investment.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside of 2‑3× the current price versus a maximum loss of 100% of the invested capital. The asymmetry is clearly in favor of a bullish stance if the catalyst materialises.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a clear catalyst confirmation (e.g., positive drilling report). Allocate 5‑10% of the portfolio, set a stop 20% below the entry point, and trail the stop as the price moves higher.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for either a drilling milestone, loan approval, or a volume spike. Once the price breaks above the 20‑day MA with volume > 2× the 5‑day average, consider a small entry to test the move.
playbook.if_passing: Not applicable – there are no immediate delisting or bankruptcy signals. The setup remains bullish as long as the company continues to secure funding and demonstrate progress.

ai_insights.bottom_line: KRPZ is a deeply crashed phosphate developer with a silent market; recent project progress and potential funding give a contrarian bullish case for a sizeable bounce, offering upside that far outweighs the limited downside risk.
